target_customer: Patients with Huntington's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders; pharma partners (licensing)
problem: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Huntington's are caused by toxic proteins that existing drugs do not remove.
business_model: Biotech drug discovery; licensing and collaboration deals

founders.name: Beth Hoffman
education: Johns Hopkins University, PhD Cell Biology
founders.background_notes: R&D executive on 30+ clinical programs in neurology, pain and psychiatry and four marketed cystic fibrosis drugs (YC page).

technical_complexity.rationale: Drug discovery for 'undruggable' neurological targets with brain penetration is research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary disease models and patentable small molecules; clinical-stage biotech assets are hard to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ipsen obtained an exclusive option to license a research program (announced 2026-01-30; terms not disclosed).

market_need_then: Huntington's disease is fatal and progressive with no disease-modifying therapy (company description); no sourced market sizing.

identity.logo: Color and white-on-dark versions of an Origami Therapeutics logo (design not described)

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive word, but no brand-specific evidence; biotech brands rarely drive outcomes.

outcome_analysis: Origami Therapeutics, a Huntington's protein-degrader biotech founded in 2015 and in YC Winter 2022, is still active. Its one verifiable milestone is Ipsen's exclusive option to license a research program (January 2026), which is a partnering validation, but no financing rounds are public in the sources reached, so progress cannot be compared with funding.
